rule1.explanation: S1 and S2 are not contraries. S1 and S2 are antonyms.

rule6.explanation: ~S1 and ~S2 are not contraries. They are both false, but ~S1 implies S2, not ~S2.

rule1.explanation: Essence and Existence can both hold together (e.g., a living being has essence and existence), both fail together (e.g., a non-living being has neither essence nor existence), or one can hold alone (e.g., a concept has essence but no existence, or a phenomenon has existence but no essence).

rule2.explanation: Essence and Essentiality are contradictories (e.g., something is either essential or not essential, but not both).

rule3.explanation: Existence and Non-Existent are contradictories (e.g., something is either existent or not existent, but not both).

rule4.explanation: ~S2 (Non-Existent) implies S1 (Essence) because if something does not exist, it may still have an essence or concept.

rule5.explanation: ~S1 (Essentiality) does not imply S2 (Existence) because something can have essentiality without existing (e.g., a concept or an idea).

rule6.explanation: ~S1 (Essentiality) and ~S2 (Non-Existent) are not contraries because they do not have the same relationship as S1 and S2 (e.g., something can be essential but not existent, or not essential but existent).

rule1.explanation: Verisimilitude and pretension are contraries, as they can hold together or fail together, and one can hold alone.

rule2.explanation: Verisimilitude and unverisimilitude are contradictories, as they cannot hold together.

rule3.explanation: Pretension and authenticity are contradictories, as they cannot hold together.

rule4.explanation: ~S2 (Authenticity) does not imply S1 (verisimilitude), as authenticity does not necessarily require verisimilitude.

rule5.explanation: ~S1 (Unverisimilitude) does not imply S2 (pretension), as unverisimilitude does not necessarily require pretension.

rule6.explanation: ~S1 (Unverisimilitude) and ~S2 (Authenticity) are contraries, as they can hold together or fail together, and one can hold alone.

rule1.explanation: Persistence and Transience are antonyms, not contraries.

rule2.explanation: Persistence and Endurance are indeed contradictories.

rule3.explanation: Transience and Permanence are indeed contradictories.

rule4.explanation: ~S2 (Permanence) implies S1 (Persistence), as Permanence implies something remains, which is Persistence.

rule5.explanation: ~S1 (Endurance) implies S2 (Transience), as Endurance implies something lasts, which is not Transience.

rule6.explanation: ~S1 (Endurance) and ~S2 (Permanence) are not contraries, they are contradictories.

rule1.explanation: Unmanifest and Illusory can hold together (e.g. an illusion that doesn't exist) or fail together (e.g. an illusion that doesn't exist and doesn't manifest), and one can hold alone (e.g. something that doesn't exist but is real)

rule2.explanation: ~S2 (Manifest Reality) and S1 (Unmanifest) are not contradictories, as they can coexist (e.g. a real, existing thing that is not manifest)

rule3.explanation: ~S2 (Manifest Reality) and S2 (Illusory) are not contradictories, as they can coexist (e.g. a real, existing thing that is an illusion)

rule4.explanation: ~S2 (Manifest Reality) implies S1 (Unmanifest), as something that is manifest cannot be unmanifest

rule5.explanation: ~S1 (Essential Manifestation) implies S2 (Illusory), as something that is essential cannot be illusory

rule6.explanation: ~S1 (Essential Manifestation) and ~S2 (Manifest Reality) are not contraries, as they can coexist (e.g. something that is essential but not manifest)
